325	/**
326	 * Restore an item from the recycle bin back to a folder.
327	 *
328	 * Removes the entry from bin metadata, adds the preserved FolderChild
329	 * back to the target folder's children, and publishes both.
330	 */
331	export async function restoreFromBin(params: {
332	  entryId: string;
333	  targetFolderIpnsName: string;
334	  folderTree: FolderTree;
335	  binState: BinState;
336	  binCtx: BinOperationContext;
337	}): Promise<{ restoredItem: FolderChild; updatedBinState: BinState }> {
338	  // 1. Find the bin entry
339	  const entry = params.binState.entries.find((e) => e.id === params.entryId);
340	  if (!entry) throw new Error('Bin entry not found');
341	
342	  // 2. Get the FolderChild to restore
343	  let child: FolderChild;
344	  if (entry.itemType === 'file' && entry.filePointer) {
345	    child = { ...entry.filePointer, modifiedAt: Date.now() };
346	  } else if (entry.itemType === 'folder' && entry.folderEntry) {
347	    child = { ...entry.folderEntry, modifiedAt: Date.now() };
348	  } else {
349	    throw new Error('Bin entry has no stored item reference');
350	  }
351	
352	  // 3. Add child back to target folder
353	  const targetFolder = params.folderTree.get(params.targetFolderIpnsName);
354	  if (!targetFolder) throw new Error('Target folder not loaded');
355	
356	  // A retry of a partially-applied restore (the bin entry survives a step-5b /
357	  // step-6 failure) can find this child already listed in the target from the prior
358	  // attempt's publish. Drop any prior copy by id so the restore is idempotent —
359	  // re-running REPLACES rather than duplicates the listing — and exclude it from the
360	  // name-collision check so the file isn't spuriously renamed against itself. The
361	  // no-conflict publish path doesn't dedup by id (only the 409 merge does), so a
362	  // same-id duplicate appended here would otherwise persist.
363	  const targetChildrenSansChild = targetFolder.children.filter((c) => c.id !== child.id);
364	
365	  // Handle name collisions (against other entries only)
366	  const existingNames = new Set(targetChildrenSansChild.map((c) => c.name));
367	  if (existingNames.has(child.name)) {
368	    let newName = `${child.name} (restored)`;
369	    let counter = 2;
370	    while (existingNames.has(newName)) {
371	      newName = `${child.name} (restored ${counter})`;
372	      counter++;
373	    }
374	    child = { ...child, name: newName };
375	  }
376	
377	  // 3b. Decide whether this restore must re-encrypt the file's FileMetadata to
378	  // the target folderKey: only for a FILE restored to a DIFFERENT folder than its
379	  // original parent. The record is AES-256-GCM sealed with the parent folderKey,
380	  // and addToBin stores the FilePointer verbatim without re-keying; restoring to a
381	  // folder with a different folderKey without re-encrypting would make the file
382	  // undecryptable (CryptoError: Decryption failed) — the same class of bug as
383	  // moveItem. Restoring in place (target === original parent, the default UI flow)
384	  // leaves the key unchanged, so no re-encrypt is needed.
385	  //
386	  // Validate the preconditions NOW, before publishing, so a restore that is
387	  // guaranteed to fail (missing file IPNS key, or a legacy entry whose source key
388	  // can't be recovered) aborts cleanly without leaving an undecryptable listing in
389	  // the target. The actual re-key — unwrap + network resolve/publish — runs AFTER
390	  // the target folder is durably published (step 5b), mirroring moveItem: the
391	  // metadata is only re-keyed once the target listing is durable, so at every
392	  // intermediate failure the file stays readable from somewhere that lists it under
393	  // the matching key (the bin, by the source key, before the re-key; the target, by
394	  // the target key, after it) — never readable from neither.
395	  const mustReencrypt =
396	    entry.itemType === 'file' &&
397	    !!entry.filePointer &&
398	    params.targetFolderIpnsName !== entry.originalParentIpnsName;
399	  if (mustReencrypt) {
400	    if (!entry.filePointer!.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted) {
401	      throw new Error('Cannot re-encrypt file metadata on restore: missing file IPNS key');
402	    }
403	    // Source key = the folderKey the FileMetadata is currently sealed under.
404	    // Recoverable from the key captured at delete time (works even if the original
405	    // parent is gone), or — for legacy entries created before that capture — from
406	    // the still-loaded original parent folder.
407	    if (!entry.originalFolderKeyEncrypted && !params.folderTree.get(entry.originalParentIpnsName)) {
408	      throw new Error(
409	        'Original parent folder must be loaded to restore a legacy file to a different folder'
410	      );
411	    }
412	  }
413	
414	  const baseChildren = [...targetFolder.children];
415	  const updatedFolderChildren = [...targetChildrenSansChild, child];
416	
417	  // 4. Publish target folder first (add-before-remove): the file is listed in the
418	  //    target while still recorded in the bin, so it is never lost mid-restore.
419	  const { newSequenceNumber, publishedChildren } = await sdkCore.updateFolderMetadataAndPublish({
420	    children: updatedFolderChildren,
421	    baseChildren,
422	    folderKey: targetFolder.folderKey,
423	    ipnsPrivateKey: targetFolder.ipnsKeypair.privateKey,
424	    ipnsName: params.targetFolderIpnsName,
425	    sequenceNumber: targetFolder.sequenceNumber,
426	    ctx: params.binCtx.ctx,
427	  });
428	
429	  // 5. Update folder state — adopt merged published set (CR-01)
430	  targetFolder.children = publishedChildren;
431	  targetFolder.sequenceNumber = newSequenceNumber;
432	  targetFolder.lastLoadedAt = Date.now();
433	  params.folderTree.set(params.targetFolderIpnsName, targetFolder);
434	
435	  // 5b. Re-key the FileMetadata to the target folderKey, now that the target
436	  //     listing is durable (see step 3b). Idempotent via
437	  //     reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange: a retry after a partial failure that
438	  //     already re-keyed the record completes cleanly instead of throwing.
439	  if (mustReencrypt) {
440	    // Only freshly-unwrapped key material is cleared in `finally` — never the
441	    // shared folderTree key from the legacy fallback, which the tree still owns.
442	    let unwrappedSourceFolderKey: Uint8Array | undefined;
443	    let fileIpnsPrivateKey: Uint8Array | undefined;
444	    try {
445	      // Both guaranteed by the precondition check above; re-narrowed here for the
446	      // type-checker and as defense in depth.
447	      const filePointer = entry.filePointer;
448	      const ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted = filePointer?.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted;
449	      if (!filePointer || !ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted) {
450	        throw new Error('Cannot re-encrypt file metadata on restore: missing file IPNS key');
451	      }
452	
453	      let sourceFolderKey: Uint8Array;
454	      if (entry.originalFolderKeyEncrypted) {
455	        unwrappedSourceFolderKey = await unwrapKey(
456	          hexToBytes(entry.originalFolderKeyEncrypted),
457	          params.binCtx.userPrivateKey
458	        );
459	        sourceFolderKey = unwrappedSourceFolderKey;
460	      } else {
461	        const sourceFolder = params.folderTree.get(entry.originalParentIpnsName);
462	        if (!sourceFolder) {
463	          throw new Error(
464	            'Original parent folder must be loaded to restore a legacy file to a different folder'
465	          );
466	        }
467	        sourceFolderKey = sourceFolder.folderKey;
468	      }
469	
470	      fileIpnsPrivateKey = await unwrapKey(
471	        hexToBytes(ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted),
472	        params.binCtx.userPrivateKey
473	      );
474	      await reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange({
475	        fileMetaIpnsName: filePointer.fileMetaIpnsName,
476	        fileIpnsPrivateKey,
477	        sourceFolderKey,
478	        destFolderKey: targetFolder.folderKey,
479	        ctx: params.binCtx.ctx,
480	      });
481	    } finally {
482	      if (unwrappedSourceFolderKey) clearBytes(unwrappedSourceFolderKey);
483	      if (fileIpnsPrivateKey) clearBytes(fileIpnsPrivateKey);
484	    }
485	  }
486	
487	  // 6. Remove entry from bin and publish
488	  const remainingEntries = params.binState.entries.filter((e) => e.id !== params.entryId);
489	  const newBinSeq = params.binState.sequenceNumber + 1;
490	
491	  const metadata: RecycleBinMetadata = {
492	    version: BIN_METADATA_VERSION,
493	    sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
494	    entries: remainingEntries,
495	  };
496	
497	  await saveBinMetadata({ metadata, binCtx: params.binCtx });
498	
499	  const updatedBinState: BinState = {
500	    entries: remainingEntries,
501	    sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
502	    ipnsName: params.binState.ipnsName,
503	  };
504	
505	  return { restoredItem: child, updatedBinState };
506	}

510	 *
511	 * For files: unpins the content CID if available.
512	 * Does NOT handle recursive folder cleanup (that requires deep IPNS traversal).
513	 */
514	export async function permanentDeleteFromBin(params: {
515	  entryId: string;
516	  binState: BinState;
517	  binCtx: BinOperationContext;
518	}): Promise<{ updatedBinState: BinState }> {
519	  const entry = params.binState.entries.find((e) => e.id === params.entryId);
520	  if (!entry) throw new Error('Bin entry not found');

526	    } catch {
527	      // Best-effort CID cleanup
528	    }
529	  }
530	
531	  // Remove from bin metadata and publish
532	  const remainingEntries = params.binState.entries.filter((e) => e.id !== params.entryId);
533	  const newBinSeq = params.binState.sequenceNumber + 1;
534	
535	  const metadata: RecycleBinMetadata = {
536	    version: BIN_METADATA_VERSION,
537	    sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
538	    entries: remainingEntries,
539	  };
540	
541	  await saveBinMetadata({ metadata, binCtx: params.binCtx });
542	
543	  return {
544	    updatedBinState: {

546	      sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
547	      ipnsName: params.binState.ipnsName,
548	    },
549	  };
550	}
551	
552	/**
553	 * Empty the bin by permanently deleting all entries.
554	 *
555	 * Cleans up CIDs (best-effort) and publishes empty bin metadata.
556	 */
557	export async function emptyBin(params: {
558	  binState: BinState;
559	  binCtx: BinOperationContext;
560	}): Promise<{ updatedBinState: BinState }> {
561	  // Best-effort CID cleanup for each entry
562	  for (const entry of params.binState.entries) {
563	    if (entry.contentCid) {
564	      try {
565	        await sdkCore.unpinFromIpfs(params.binCtx.ctx, entry.contentCid);
566	      } catch {
567	        // Non-blocking
568	      }
569	    }
570	  }
571	
572	  // Publish empty bin metadata
573	  const newBinSeq = params.binState.sequenceNumber + 1;
574	  const metadata: RecycleBinMetadata = {
575	    version: BIN_METADATA_VERSION,
576	    sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
577	    entries: [],
578	  };
579	
580	  await saveBinMetadata({ metadata, binCtx: params.binCtx });
581	
582	  return {
583	    updatedBinState: {
584	      entries: [],
585	      sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
586	      ipnsName: params.binState.ipnsName,
587	    },
588	  };
589	}

591	/**
592	 * Purge expired bin entries based on retention period.
593	 *
594	 * Filters entries past their retention, cleans up CIDs (best-effort),
595	 * and publishes updated bin metadata in a single IPNS publish.
596	 *
597	 * @returns Number of purged entries and updated bin state
598	 */
599	export async function purgeExpiredEntries(params: {
600	  binState: BinState;
601	  retentionDays: number;
602	  binCtx: BinOperationContext;
603	}): Promise<{ purgedCount: number; updatedState: BinState }> {
604	  const retentionMs = params.retentionDays * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
605	  const now = Date.now();
606	
607	  const expired = params.binState.entries.filter((e) => now - e.deletedAt > retentionMs);
608	  if (expired.length === 0) {
609	    return { purgedCount: 0, updatedState: params.binState };
610	  }
611	
612	  // Remove expired entries and publish updated bin BEFORE cleanup.
613	  // This ensures bin metadata is consistent even if CID unpins fail.
614	  const expiredIds = new Set(expired.map((e) => e.id));
615	  const remainingEntries = params.binState.entries.filter((e) => !expiredIds.has(e.id));
616	  const newBinSeq = params.binState.sequenceNumber + 1;
617	
618	  const metadata: RecycleBinMetadata = {
619	    version: BIN_METADATA_VERSION,
620	    sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
621	    entries: remainingEntries,
622	  };
623	
624	  await saveBinMetadata({ metadata, binCtx: params.binCtx });
625	
626	  // Best-effort CID cleanup for expired entries (after metadata is saved)
627	  for (const entry of expired) {
628	    if (entry.contentCid) {
629	      try {
630	        await sdkCore.unpinFromIpfs(params.binCtx.ctx, entry.contentCid);
631	      } catch {
632	        // Best-effort: CID cleanup failures are non-blocking
633	      }
634	    }
635	    // Also clean up version CIDs to recover quota
636	    if (entry.versionCids) {
637	      for (const vc of entry.versionCids) {
638	        try {
639	          await sdkCore.unpinFromIpfs(params.binCtx.ctx, vc.cid);
640	        } catch {
641	          // Best-effort
642	        }
643	      }
644	    }
645	  }
646	
647	  return {
648	    purgedCount: expired.length,
649	    updatedState: {
650	      entries: remainingEntries,
651	      sequenceNumber: newBinSeq,
652	      ipnsName: params.binState.ipnsName,
653	    },
654	  };
655	}

> AGENT

I've now read the full bin module. Here's the brainstorm, grounded in the actual code.

## What's actually broken (it's worse than "addToBin doesn't capture")

There are **two** layers of defect:

1. **`addToBin` (L290-302) never captures** `contentCid` / `contentSize` / `versionCids`. It stores `filePointer` (which only has `fileMetaIpnsName`) and sets `size: 0`. The real content CID lives one hop away, inside the file's own encrypted `FileMetadata` (`.cid` + `.versions[].cid`), which `addToBin` never resolves.

2. **The three cleanup paths are inconsistent**, and all three are starved of data:
   - `permanentDeleteFromBin` (L523) — unpins **only** `contentCid`, **doesn't even loop `versionCids`**.
   - `emptyBin` (L563) — same, **only** `contentCid`, no version loop.
   - `purgeExpiredEntries` (L628-644) — correctly loops **both** `contentCid` and `versionCids`.

So even if you back-filled `versionCids` today, two of the three paths would still leak every version. The fix has to touch both layers.

## My recommended approach

**Capture at delete time, in `addToBin`** (the todo's option 1) — and I'd commit to it over lazy-resolve-at-empty for a concrete reason: once a file is soft-deleted it's removed from the folder, and its own IPNS record is no longer something we keep alive. Resolving lazily at empty-time risks the file's IPNS record having aged out → unresolvable → permanent leak. Capturing at delete time snapshots the CIDs while the file is still fully wired, and amortizes one resolve per delete instead of N resolves per empty.

Concretely:
- In `addToBin`, for files, resolve `filePointer.fileMetaIpnsName` → fetch+decrypt `FileMetadata` with `folder.folderKey` (which `addToBin` already has in hand — it wraps it for restore at L268), and populate `contentCid`, `contentSize`, `versionCids`.
- Make `permanentDeleteFromBin` and `emptyBin` loop `versionCids` exactly like `purgeExpiredEntries` already does — ideally factor the per-entry "unpin contentCid + all versionCids (best-effort)" into one shared helper so the three paths can't drift again.

## Design decisions worth your call

**Failure handling in `addToBin`:** resolve the FileMetadata **early** (before the folder publish, while the file is maximally reachable) but treat a resolve/decrypt failure as **best-effort** — log and proceed with `contentCid` undefined rather than blocking the delete. The delete is the user's intent; CID capture is bookkeeping, and `filePointer` is still stored so a future sweep could retry. Fail-closed here would mean a transient IPNS hiccup blocks deleting a file — wrong tradeoff.

**Scope: drop item 3 (the CAS metadata-blob tail) from this PR.** Re-read the evidence numbers: the 9 content CIDs are **439 of the 442 MB**; the ~230 superseded-metadata pins are sub-10KB → ~3 MB, <1% of the leak. Unpinning the superseded folder-metadata CID on every publish is also *riskier* (must reason about concurrent readers, the 409-merge path, and the fact that `publishWithVerify` deliberately **doesn't throw** on unconfirmed propagation — unpinning the old CID after an unverified publish could 404 a reader). That's a separate correctness surface for ~1% of the bytes. I'd file it as its own todo and keep this PR to items 1, 2, 4.

**Legacy entries:** the capture-at-delete fix is forward-only — entries already sitting in users' bins stay `contentCid: undefined` and still leak on empty. I'd leave the SDK fix clean/forward-only and reclaim existing leaks via the optional staging remediation (item 5) + the GC todo, rather than bolting a lazy-resolve fallback into `emptyBin` (which reintroduces the "file IPNS aged out" fragility for exactly the oldest entries). Flagging it so it's a conscious choice.

**Test (item 4):** lead with a **unit test in `packages/sdk`** that mocks `sdkCore.unpinFromIpfs` and asserts it's invoked with `contentCid` + each `versionCid` after `addToBin → emptyBin` (and `→ permanentDeleteFromBin`). That directly pins the actual defect ("the unpin call never fires"), needs no infra, and guards the inconsistency between the three paths. Add an sdk-e2e real-quota-drop assertion only if you want the end-to-end proof too.

## Two real risks to resolve before/while implementing

1. **Shared-CID ref-counting.** If a file is shared (user-to-user or link share) and the owner deletes it + empties bin, does unpinning the content CID break the sharee? `guardedUnpin` is keyed on the owner's pubkey, but Kubo pins the block globally — if the owner's `pin rm` drops the last Kubo pin, GC can reclaim a block a sharee still references. Need to confirm whether sharees hold their own `pinned_cids` rows (independent pins) or reference the owner's. This is the one thing that could make "fix the leak" cause data loss.

2. **Intra-user dedup** is a non-issue — random AES nonces mean identical plaintext → distinct ciphertext → distinct CIDs, so a file and its versions never share a content CID. Worth one sentence in the PR but not a blocker.

---

Net recommended scope for the PR: **capture in `addToBin` + unify all three cleanup paths via a shared unpin helper + unit test**, defer the metadata-tail (item 3) and any legacy-entry sweep, and **answer the shared-CID question first** since it gates whether unpin-on-delete is even safe.

Want me to (a) spin up an Explore agent to resolve the shared-CID ref-counting question against the sharing/vault code, (b) move to a full Plan with this scope, or (c) just start implementing it?

Now I have all the evidence I need. Let me compile the final report:

## FINAL REPORT: Unpin Safety for Shared Files

Based on comprehensive code tracing of the CipherBox codebase, here are the findings:

### A. UNPIN PATH — What guardedUnpin Does

**File**: `apps/api/src/vault/vault.service.ts`, lines 247-339

The unpin process has **REFERENCE COUNTING across all users**:

1. **Ownership check** (line 269): Looks up the caller's own `(userId, cid)` row in `pinned_cids`. If not found, returns silently without touching Kubo (line 276).

2. **Row deletion** (line 280): Deletes the caller's pinned_cids row. This IS the quota decrement (in-transaction, line 279 comment).

3. **Refcount check** (lines 289-293): 
   ```typescript
   const result = await manager
     .createQueryBuilder(PinnedCid, 'pc')
     .select('COUNT(*)', 'count')
     .where('pc.cid = :cid', { cid })
     .getRawOne<{ count: string }>();
   const refcount = parseInt(result?.count ?? '0', 10);
   ```
   Counts ALL remaining `pinned_cids` rows for that CID across **ALL users** (no `userId` filter).

4. **Conditional Kubo unpin** (lines 296-306): Only if `refcount === 0`, queues a physical `pin rm` to Kubo via the `pending_unpins` outbox (lines 298-304).

5. **Post-commit Kubo call** (lines 312-330): After transaction commits, if a pending_unpin was queued, calls `this.ipfsProvider.unpinFile(cid)` which executes `POST /api/v0/pin/rm?arg={cid}` to Kubo (local.provider.ts, line 88).

**Reference counting is YES — mandatory and cross-user**.

### B. PINNED_CIDS UNIQUENESS

**File**: `apps/api/src/vault/entities/pinned-cid.entity.ts`, line 14 + migration `apps/api/src/migrations/1700000000000-FullSchema.ts`, line 129

Schema constraint: `CONSTRAINT "UQ_pinned_cids_user_cid" UNIQUE ("user_id", "cid")`

This is a **per-(user, cid) unique constraint**. Two users **CAN** independently have rows for the same CID.

Example:
- User A uploads a file → gets `pinned_cids(userA, cidX, 1000)`
- User A shares file with User B → User B reads from cidX (no new row for B)
- User A deletes to bin and calls `emptyBin` → calls `guardedUnpin(userA, cidX)` → deletes userA's row
- **Refcount for cidX is still 1** (B's row exists or it's 0 if B never pinned)

### C. SHARE PIN MODEL

**Finding**: Sharees **DO NOT create their own pinned_cids rows**.

**Evidence**:
1. Shares service (`apps/api/src/shares/shares.service.ts`): Creates only `share` and `share_key` records. Zero pinning logic.
2. Share invites service (`apps/api/src/shares/share-invite.service.ts`): Same — zero pinning on claim.
3. IPFS controller (`apps/api/src/ipfs/ipfs.controller.ts`): `recordPin` is called only in two places:
   - Line 120: After `POST /ipfs/upload` (user uploads a file)
   - Line 182: In `POST /ipfs/register-cid` (BYO users register external CIDs)
   
   Neither is triggered by share accept/claim flows.

4. SDK shared-write (`packages/sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts`): When a write-share recipient uploads a file to a shared folder, they call `addToIpfs()` which uploads via the backend's `/ipfs/upload` endpoint. This calls `recordPin` for the **uploader's userId**, not the file content owner's. For a sharee uploading in a shared folder, that's the sharee's own pin.

5. **User-to-user shares**: Sharee reads the owner's already-pinned CID via `POST /ipfs/{cid}`. Zero local pin created.

6. **Link shares (invites)**: Same — no pinning on claim.

**Verdict for shares**: Sharees reference the owner's content CID with no local pin. The owner's pinned_cids row is the ONLY tracker for that CID.

### D. VERDICT: IS OWNER UNPIN-ON-BIN-EMPTY SAFE FOR SHAREES?

**YES — BUT WITH A CRITICAL DISTINCTION**:

**For user-to-user and link shares where the sharee is only READING**: SAFE. The unpin is safe because:
- Sharee has NO pinned_cids row for the shared content CID
- When owner calls `emptyBin`, which calls `guardedUnpin(ownerUserId, contentCid)`:
  - Owner's row is deleted
  - Refcount across ALL users for that CID goes to 0 (sharee has no row to block it)
  - Kubo `pin rm` IS executed
  - **Block is removed from IPFS**
  - Sharee can NO LONGER fetch the content (Kubo `cat` fails)
  
**⚠️ OUTCOME: ORPHANING THE SHAREE** — The sharee loses access to the content. This is the data-loss risk.

**For write-share recipients who UPLOAD to the shared folder**: Write-share recipients upload via `/ipfs/upload`, which creates a LOCAL pinned_cids row under their own userId. If the sharee uploads a file to a write-shared folder and then the owner empties the bin (unpinning the sharee's own file's CID), the sharee's pin protects it. However, this is the sharee's own content, not a cross-user scenario.

### E. UNKNOWNS / GAPS

1. **Bin entry contentCid field**: The code shows BinEntry has a `contentCid?` field (optional). When a file is soft-deleted to the bin, is this field populated with the file's content CID?
   - Search results show permanentDeleteFromBin and emptyBin UNPIN it IF present (lines 523-530, 563-570 in bin/index.ts)
   - But I did NOT find where BinEntry.contentCid is SET during addToBin
   - **Answer location needed**: `packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts` addToBin function (around line 241), see if it wraps the FilePointer's metadata CID or the content CID

2. **Public link share**: The codebase has invites, but I did not trace whether CipherBox has a "public link" mode (unauthenticated sharing) separate from invite-based links. If unauthenticated access to shared files is supported, the same orphaning risk applies.
   - **Answer location**: Check if `GET /ipfs/{cid}` in ipfs.controller.ts requires auth (yes, line 47 `@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard)`), so unauthenticated public reads are NOT supported at the API level. Public shares would still route through authenticated endpoints.

3. **BYO user pinning**: BYO users can register external CIDs via `/ipfs/register-cid` (line 172, ipfs.controller.ts). If a BYO user registers a CID that another (hosted) user also pins, does the refcount include BYO rows?
   - **Answer from code**: YES. Comment WR-07 in guardedUnpin (lines 284-288) explicitly states BYO advisory rows count toward the hosted refcount. Design decision: a BYO row blocks physical unpin of hosted content.

### SUMMARY TABLE

| Scenario | Sharee Pins Content? | Owner Unpins Safe? | Risk |
|----------|-------|-------|-----|
| User-to-user read share | NO | YES (refcount = 0) | Sharee orphaned ⚠️ |
| User-to-user write share (owner unpin) | NO (owns their uploads) | YES | Sharee orphaned ⚠️ |
| Link share (invite) read | NO | YES | Sharee orphaned ⚠️ |
| Link share (invite) write | NO (owns their uploads) | YES | Sharee orphaned ⚠️ |
| BYO user pins same CID as hosted owner | YES (advisory row) | NO (refcount > 0) | Safe — BYO row blocks unpin |

**Exact risk scenario**: 
1. Owner uploads `cidX`, creates `pinned_cids(ownerID, cidX, size)`
2. Owner shares `cidX` with Sharee (no new pin created for Sharee)
3. Owner calls `emptyBin` → `permanentDeleteFromBin(cidX)` → `guardedUnpin(ownerID, cidX)`
4. Owner's row deleted, refcount = 0
5. Kubo `pin rm cidX` executed
6. Block removed from Kubo
7. Sharee calls `GET /ipfs/cidX` → Kubo returns "blockstore: block not found"
8. Share becomes unreadable; **shared file is lost for the sharee**
```

Exploration done — clear, and it confirms the risk is real. Here's the verdict.

## Finding: unpin-on-empty **will orphan sharees**

The ref-counting machinery exists but is defeated by the share model:

- **`guardedUnpin` already ref-counts across all users** (`apps/api/src/vault/vault.service.ts` ~247-339): it deletes the caller's `pinned_cids` row, then counts *all* remaining `pinned_cids` rows for that CID (no `userId` filter), and only enqueues the Kubo `pin rm` when the count hits **0**.
- **`pinned_cids` is `UNIQUE(user_id, cid)`** — two users *can* independently row the same CID, so refcounting *would* protect shared content…
- **…except sharees never get a pin row.** `shares.service.ts` and `share-invite.service.ts` have **zero** pinning logic; `recordPin` is only called on `/ipfs/upload` and `/ipfs/register-cid`. A sharee reads the owner's pinned block via `POST /ipfs/{cid}` with no pin of their own (both user-to-user and invite/link shares). All reads are authenticated (`JwtAuthGuard`), so there's no separate unauthenticated public mode.

**Exact data-loss scenario:** owner uploads `cidX` → shares it (no sharee pin created) → owner deletes to bin → `emptyBin` calls `guardedUnpin(owner, cidX)` → owner's row deleted → cross-user refcount = **0** → Kubo `pin rm cidX` → block GC'd → sharee's `GET /ipfs/cidX` returns "block not found." **Shared file lost for the sharee.**

(One edge: a *BYO* user who registered the same CID gets an advisory `pinned_cids` row that *does* count toward the refcount — WR-07 — so that one case blocks the unpin. Not the common path.)

So today's "never unpin" bug is, perversely, the only thing protecting shared files. Wiring up the unpin without a share decision would convert a quota leak into a data-loss bug for shared content.

Per your instruction, I'm not assuming the handling. How should a permanent delete (empty bin / permanent-delete / expiry purge) treat content that is currently shared?

Share-revocation exploration is back, and it changes the implementation shape — revocation here isn't a single clean delete. Key facts:

## How revocation actually works
- **Shares are keyed by `ipnsName`** — a file's `fileMetaIpnsName` or a folder's IPNS name (`Share.ipnsName`, `ShareInvite.ipnsName`). So I can enumerate everything for an item by that one key. There's **no bulk endpoint** today — the client lists sent shares + invites and revokes them one-by-one.
- **Two share kinds, two revoke paths:** user-to-user (`DELETE /shares/:id` → sets `revokedAt`) and invite/link (`DELETE /shares/invites/:id` → `status='revoked'`). A **claimed invite becomes an independent `Share` row**, so revoking the invite doesn't kill the access it already granted — but since that spawned Share is also keyed by the same `ipnsName`, enumerating all `Share` rows by `ipnsName` catches it. Good — full coverage = revoke all Shares + all active Invites for the `ipnsName`.
- **Revoke is lazy/soft, not an immediate crypto cutoff.** `revokeShare` only stamps `revokedAt`; actual key rotation + hard-delete happens on the *next modification of that folder* (`completeRotation`, CASCADE-deletes `ShareKey`s). **But a deleted item never gets a "next modification"** — so naive soft-revoke would leave the rows in permanent lazy-rotation limbo, and the recipient still holds their wrapped key. For a *deleted* item the real access cutoff is the **content unpin at empty-bin** (the ciphertext blocks vanish); key rotation is moot because there are no remaining recipients to re-wrap for.

So the coherent design: at `addToBin`, hard-revoke all Shares + Invites for the item's `ipnsName` (no rotation debt — nothing to rotate for a dead item), capture `contentCid`/`versionCids`, and let empty-bin do the unpin that finishes the cutoff.

That leaves three genuine "how should shares be handled" forks I won't assume on:

- **Must be client-side.** The server is zero-knowledge — it can't decrypt folder metadata to enumerate descendants. - **`BinEntry` needs a new field** to carry the descendant CID list (a metadata-schema bump, `BinEntry.descendantCids` or similar) so empty-bin can unpin the whole subtree.
- **Partial-failure ordering** (walk → revoke → remove-from-parent → publish bin) becomes a real design point — but a transactional bulk revoke shrinks the bad-state window.

All four decisions locked. Here's the consolidated spec for the brainstorm — one PR, full scope.

## Locked design

**Behavior**
- Soft-delete (`addToBin`) revokes the item's shares; revoke is **one-way** (restore does not resurrect shares).
- Folder delete **traverses the whole deleted subtree** and revokes every share/invite on the folder + descendants.
- Revocation goes through a **new atomic bulk endpoint** taking the list of `ipnsName`s the client collected.
- Empty-bin / permanent-delete / purge **unpin** content + version + descendant CIDs (the actual access cutoff + quota reclaim).

**Change set (one PR)**

1. **Client subtree walk** (sdk/sdk-core, new helper) — given a folder, recursively resolve+decrypt descendant folder metadata and collect, in one pass: every descendant file's `contentCid`/`versionCids` (for unpin) **and** every node's `ipnsName` (folder + descendant files + subfolders, for revoke). Server can't do this — zero-knowledge — so it's client-side with the folder keys.

2. **`addToBin`** (`packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:241`) — file path: resolve `fileMetaIpnsName` → decrypt `FileMetadata` with `folder.folderKey` (already in hand at L268) → capture `contentCid`/`contentSize`/`versionCids` + revoke the file's own shares. Folder path: run the walk → store descendant CIDs on the entry + bulk-revoke all collected `ipnsName`s. Capture/walk happens **before** the folder publish so a failure aborts cleanly.

3. **`BinEntry` schema** (`packages/core/src/bin/types.ts`) — add `descendantCids?: Array<{cid; size}>`. Additive/optional → backward-compatible, stays `v1`.

4. **Unpin unification** (`bin/index.ts`) — one `unpinEntryCids(ctx, entry)` helper (content + every version + every descendant, each best-effort) called by `emptyBin`, `permanentDeleteFromBin`, **and** `purgeExpiredEntries` — fixes the current bug where the first two don't even loop `versionCids`.

5. **Bulk revoke endpoint** (`apps/api/src/shares`) — `POST /shares/revoke-for-items { ipnsNames: string[] }` → for the authed sharer, in one transaction: hard-remove all `Share` rows (CASCADE `ShareKey`) and revoke all `ShareInvite` rows where `sharerId = caller AND ipnsName IN (list)`. Matching by `ipnsName` also catches claimed-invite-derived Shares. DTO + service + controller + spec, then `pnpm api:generate`.

6. **Client revoke wiring** — SDK `revokeSharesForItems(ipnsNames)` → new api-client call; `addToBin` invokes it.

7. **Tests** — unit (sdk): file-delete→empty asserts unpin of content+versions; folder-delete→empty asserts unpin of all descendant CIDs; addToBin asserts bulk-revoke called with the right `ipnsName`s. API: bulk-revoke spec.

**Deferred to follow-up todos** (out of this PR): the CAS metadata-blob tail (item 3, <1% of bytes, riskier) and the optional staging 442 MB remediation (item 5).

**My recommended resolutions for the remaining implementation-level points** (vetoable):
- **Walk failure policy:** fail-closed for the **share** set (a missed descendant = an un-revoked share = the exact data-leak we're closing), best-effort for the **CID** capture (a missed CID just leaks quota, recoverable later). So if the walk can't fully enumerate, abort the delete rather than half-revoke.
- **Bulk endpoint:** **hard-delete**, not soft `revokedAt` — a deleted item has no remaining recipients to lazily rotate for, so soft-revoke would just strand rows in permanent rotation limbo.
- **Ordering:** revoke **after** the folder is durably removed from its parent but **before** the bin publish, so the item is gone from the vault before access is cut (avoids "shares revoked but file still visible to owner").

This touches unpin (data-loss-adjacent) **and** access control (share revocation), so it's exactly the durability/crypto class where a thorough review pays off.

**Recommendation:** implement as one PR in a background agent, then run an adversarial verification pass (like #562) before merge. I'll fold the updated design into the todo's Solution on the same branch. Want me to kick that off?

 ## Problem
@@ -55,16 +56,48 @@ forever, while their vault/bin look empty.
 
 ## Solution
 
-1. `addToBin` must resolve and store the file's `contentCid` (`FileMetadata.cid`) and `versionCids`
-   (`FileMetadata.versions[].cid`) into the `BinEntry` at delete time.
-2. `emptyBin` / `permanentDeleteFromBin` / `purgeExpiredEntries` must unpin `contentCid` AND every
-   `versionCid` (not just the guarded `contentCid`).
-3. Consider unpinning the superseded metadata CID on CAS publish to stop metadata-blob accumulation.
-4. Add an SDK or E2E test that asserts quota drops after empty-bin (upload, delete-to-bin, empty,
-   re-read quota → released).
-5. Optional one-off staging remediation: reclaim this user's 442 MB by deleting the orphaned
-   `pinned_cids` rows + Kubo unpin, after confirming the 9 big CIDs are unreachable from the user's
-   current IPNS metadata (needs client keys, so the user must confirm the files are truly gone).
+Shipped as ONE PR (`fix(bin): unpin deleted content and revoke its shares`). Items 1, 2 and 4
+implemented; the share-revocation safety net was added because once empty-bin actually unpins, an
+unpin of a still-shared content CID would orphan the sharee (sharees never get their own
+`pinned_cids` row, so the only thing protecting shared content today is the unpin never firing).
+Items 3 and 5 are deferred to separate follow-up todos.

=== new DTO ===
import { ApiProperty } from '@nestjs/swagger';
import { IsArray, ArrayNotEmpty, ArrayMaxSize, IsString, MaxLength } from 'class-validator';

/**
 * Bulk hard-revoke request: revoke every share/invite the authenticated user
 * created for ANY of the listed IPNS names. Used when an owner deletes an item
 * (file or folder) to the recycle bin — the client collects every node ipnsName
 * in the deleted subtree (the folder's own ipnsName + every descendant file's
 * fileMetaIpnsName + every descendant subfolder ipnsName) and sends them here so
 * the access cutoff happens BEFORE the eventual unpin orphans any sharee.
 *
 * The list may contain ipnsNames that were never shared — the endpoint revokes
 * whatever matches and no-ops the rest.
 */
export class RevokeForItemsDto {
  @ApiProperty({
    description:
      'IPNS names (k51...) of every node in the deleted subtree. Shares/invites ' +
      'the caller created for any of these are hard-revoked. Unshared names are ignored.',
    type: [String],
    example: ['k51qzi5uqu5dg...', 'k51qzi5uqu5dh...'],
  })
  @IsArray()
  @ArrayNotEmpty()
  // Bound the batch so a single request can't enumerate an unbounded subtree.
  // 5000 comfortably covers realistic vault subtrees while capping DB IN(...) size.
  @ArrayMaxSize(5000)
  @IsString({ each: true })
  @MaxLength(255, { each: true })
  ipnsNames!: string[];
}

## Efficiency Review of PR #563

Based on my analysis of the diff and implementation files, here are the efficiency findings:

**packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:**

- **Line 276 (walkDeletedSubtree loop)**: `captureFileCids` is awaited **sequentially per sibling file within each folder's children loop** — all `resolveFileMetadata` calls on files in the same directory are serialized when they could run **concurrently with Promise.all**. Cost: O(n_files) network latency instead of O(1) or O(log n) with batching. Folder recursion is also sequential (line 287). Magnitude: High for large deleted subtrees with many sibling files.

- **Line 318-324 (unpinEntryCids loop)**: CID unpins are awaited one-by-one via `await sdkCore.unpinFromIpfs(ctx, cid)` in a for loop, when each unpin is **independent and fail-closed** (try/catch). Could use `Promise.all()` or `Promise.allSettled()` to parallelize unpins across the cid array. Magnitude: Medium (unpin I/O, not critical path since it's best-effort, but measurable on large bins).

- **Line 791-792 (emptyBin)** & **Line 851-852 (purgeExpiredEntries)**: Each `unpinEntryCids` call awaits its internal cid loop sequentially; the outer loop over **entries also serializes each entry's unpins** when independent entries' CID sets could all unpin in parallel. Use `Promise.all(entries.map(e => unpinEntryCids(...)))`. Magnitude: Medium-high depending on bin size.

**apps/api/src/shares/shares.service.ts:**

- **Line 309-313 (revokeForItems)**: `manager.find(Share, ...)` loads shares **then `manager.remove(shares)` removes them one-by-one inside the ORM loop** — safe by design (CASCADE on relation), but worth noting. No N+1 or duplicate query, so this is correct; not an efficiency waste. The invite QB update (lines 317-324) is properly set-based, not looped.

**Summary:**

Two clear wins: (1) parallelize `captureFileCids` per-file within each folder's children via `Promise.all`, (2) parallelize unpins via `Promise.allSettled` instead of serial `await` loops. Both preserve fail-closed/best-effort semantics. No code bugs found; only hot-path concurrency losses.

## Analysis

Looking at the diff for unnecessary complexity:

1. **File CID capture: array unpacking is verbose** (packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts, addToBin lines ~470-485)
   - The code captures `captureFileCids` return, then unpacks it: `cids[0]` → `fileContentCid` + `fileContentSize`, then `cids.slice(1)` → `fileVersionCids`
   - This is written inline instead of having `captureFileCids` return a labeled result, forcing manual indexing

2. **Retry/backoff in revokeSharesForItems** (packages/sdk/src/share/index.ts lines 160-182)
   - The function hard-codes `maxAttempts ?? 3` with exponential backoff (`300 * Math.pow(2, attempt)`)
   - For a single fail-closed call (not retried at SDK layer), this is overbuilt — SDK already wraps the call once, and the retry burden doubles handler code
   - Compare: `revokeShare` (line ~140) has NO retry logic; this one adds retry+backoff for a single endpoint that's already behind HTTP/network resilience

3. **Redundant state across BinEntry** (packages/core/src/bin/types.ts)
   - `contentCid`, `versionCids` for files; `descendantCids` for folders
   - But the diff shows: for files, `versionCids` contains ALL versions (already post-content index 0); for folders, `descendantCids` contains ALL content+versions flattened
   - **No actual redundancy here**, they're mutually exclusive (files use first two; folders use third)

4. **De-duplication in revokeForItems** (apps/api/src/shares/shares.service.ts line 301)
   - Uses `[...new Set(ipnsNames)]` — fine, but the client (`revokeSharesForItems` in share/index.ts) does NOT de-dupe before calling `revokeFn`
   - The de-dup happens only server-side; if the caller sends duplicates, the SDK has already retained them through the retry loop and the walk

5. **unpinEntryCids array assembly** (packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts lines 312-325)
   - Manually builds `cids` array by pushing conditional entries, then loops it
   - Could inline the loop (push & unpin in one pass) to avoid intermediate array

6. **walkDeletedSubtree visited set overhead** (packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts)
   - Uses a `visited` Set for cycle detection, correctly passed through recursion
   - No redundancy; necessary for safety against diamonds in client-supplied metadata

---

## Summary (tight bullet list, ~250 words max)

- **packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:~470–485 — File CID unpacking** — Calls `captureFileCids()` then manually indexes returned array (`cids[0]` → `fileContentCid`, `cids.slice(1)` → `fileVersionCids`). **Simpler:** Have `captureFileCids` return `{ contentCid?: CapturedCid; versionCids?: CapturedCid[] }` or destructure directly without intermediate `cids` array. **Cost:** Tiny (one function return shape change); improves readability & eliminates indexing fragility. ✓ BEHAVIOR SAFE.

- **packages/sdk/src/share/index.ts:160–182 — Retry + backoff overbuilt** — Adds exponential backoff + 3 retries to a single endpoint call that's already behind HTTP resilience. Compare `revokeShare` (no retry). **Simpler:** Remove backoff; let caller (addToBin) decide retry policy if needed, or rely on HTTP client. **Cost:** Removes ~8 lines; trade-off: loosens transient-failure tolerance (but HTTP already has it). ⚠ BEHAVIOR CHANGE (fewer retries); verify via integration test that staging uptime justifies removal.

- **packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:312–325 — unpinEntryCids array assembly** — Builds intermediate `cids[]` array, then loops. **Simpler:** Inline three loops (contentCid, versionCids, descendantCids) directly in unpin loop, no intermediate array. **Cost:** Saves ~5 lines; negligible perf (small entry counts). ✓ BEHAVIOR SAFE.

- **Ordering & fail-closed safety** — All present and locked (walk → revoke → publish → bin); no simplification without risk.

**packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:235-251 — walkDeletedSubtree vs collectSubtreeIpnsNamesAsync**
- **Status:** CORRECTLY NOT REUSED. Both walk subtrees but have **different fail policies**: 
  - `walkDeletedSubtree`: **FAIL-CLOSED on structure** (throws if a folder won't resolve → entire delete aborts → shares guaranteed complete before unpin).
  - `collectSubtreeIpnsNamesAsync` (client.ts:321): **Best-effort** per child (catches unwrap/fetch failures independently, logs, continues with siblings for fire-and-forget unenroll).

- **Conclusion:** Do NOT merge. Different semantics lock the correctness model.

**packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:312-323 — unpinEntryCids helper**
- **Status:** GOOD REUSE. Consolidates best-effort unpin loops that were previously duplicated inline in `emptyBin`, `permanentDeleteFromBin`, and `purgeExpiredEntries` (each had try/catch loops). Now single call, called 3 times.
- **Cost:** Eliminates ~45 LOC duplication via one 12-LOC helper.

**apps/api/src/shares/shares.service.ts:410-447 — revokeForItems transaction**
- **Status:** FOLLOWS PATTERN. Uses `dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => { ... })` consistent with vault-service.ts and share-invite-service.ts. No duplication.

---

### Summary

One low-hanging reuse opportunity: extract exponential backoff into a shared utility in `error.ts` to avoid duplication between `publishWithVerify` (500ms base) and `revokeSharesForItems` (300ms base). Subtree walk intentionally uses separate fail-closed design; do not merge. Unpin consolidation is already done well.

The four lenses converged: the code is already at the right altitude with good reuse (`unpinEntryCids` is the single chokepoint for all three purge paths; clean DI for the revoke fn; `/shares/revoke-for-items` is the correct atomic server primitive). The suggestions that came back are all ones I should **not** apply on an already-verified PR:

- **Retry-backoff DRY** (`revokeSharesForItems` vs `publishWithVerify`) — extracting a shared helper means editing the pre-existing verified publish path; out of scope, and the retry itself is locked fail-closed design.
- **Parallelize `walkDeletedSubtree`** — would race the shared `visited` cycle-guard Set, change fail-closed timing, and fire N concurrent `resolveFileMetadata` straight into the API's `ThrottlerGuard`. Not worth it on a non-hot delete path.
- **`captureFileCids` labeled return** — roughly complexity-neutral (just moves the content-vs-versions split into the walk), churns a verified path for no real gain.

**`/simplify` outcome: reviewed, nothing applied — code is already clean.** Moving to coderabbit cli. Verifying it's available, then running it scoped to this PR's diff.

144	/**
145	 * Bulk hard-revoke every share/invite the caller created for ANY of the given
146	 * IPNS names, with a couple of retries.
147	 *
148	 * Used when deleting a file/folder subtree to the recycle bin: the access cutoff
149	 * MUST land before the eventual empty-bin unpin, or a still-shared content CID
150	 * would orphan the sharee. This is therefore a fail-closed step — the caller
151	 * (addToBin) aborts the delete if it ultimately fails.
152	 *
153	 * The actual API call (POST /shares/revoke-for-items) is injected so this stays
154	 * mockable at the boundary and free of api-client coupling.
155	 *
156	 * @param params.ipnsNames - Every node ipnsName in the deleted subtree.

159	 */
160	export async function revokeSharesForItems(params: {
161	  ipnsNames: string[];
162	  revokeFn: (ipnsNames: string[]) => Promise<void>;
163	  maxAttempts?: number;
164	}): Promise<void> {
165	  if (params.ipnsNames.length === 0) return;
166	  const maxAttempts = params.maxAttempts ?? 3;
167	  let lastErr: unknown;
168	  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxAttempts; attempt++) {
169	    try {
170	      await params.revokeFn(params.ipnsNames);
171	      return;
172	    } catch (err) {
173	      lastErr = err;
174	      if (attempt < maxAttempts - 1) {
175	        await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 300 * Math.pow(2, attempt)));
176	      }
177	    }
178	  }
179	  throw lastErr instanceof Error
180	    ? lastErr
181	    : new Error('Failed to revoke shares for deleted items', { cause: lastErr });
182	}

Perfect. Now I have a complete picture. Let me create the findings report:

## FINDINGS REPORT: Desktop FUSE Delete vs. Share Revocation

**ANSWER: NO — Desktop FUSE delete BYPASSES share revocation entirely.**

### 1. Desktop Delete Path (FUSE)

**Files & Functions:**
- `crates/fuse/src/write_ops/implementation/delete.rs:58` — `handle_unlink()` (file delete)
- `crates/fuse/src/write_ops/implementation/delete.rs:208` — `handle_rmdir()` (folder delete)
- Both call `publish_bin_entry_on_delete()` (line 16), which spawns `spawn_bin_entry_publish()` 

**Execution flow:**
1. FUSE callback (macOS SMB mount or Linux FUSE) receives unlink/rmdir
2. Rust FUSE handler (`handle_unlink`/`handle_rmdir`) removes inode, updates parent metadata, publishes updated parent to IPNS
3. Calls `spawn_bin_entry_publish()` to publish a single BinEntry to the bin IPNS record
4. Returns success to filesystem

**Does it call `addToBin`?** NO — it is a parallel Rust-only implementation.

---

### 2. SDK Client Delete Path (Web)

**Files & Functions:**
- `packages/sdk/src/client.ts:1930` — calls `addToBin()` with `revokeSharesForItemsFn` injected
- `packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:413` — `addToBin()` orchestrates the delete with share revocation

**Execution flow (critical ordering):**
1. Walk deleted subtree to collect all ipnsNames (fail-closed if unreadable)
2. Call `revokeSharesForItemsFn((ipnsNames) => this.revokeSharesForItems(ipnsNames))`
3. This issues `POST /shares/revoke-for-items` (packages/sdk/src/client.ts:226)
4. **ONLY AFTER** share revocation succeeds, mutate folder + publish + create BinEntry

**Does FUSE reach this?** NO — the Rust FUSE crate (`crates/fuse`) has zero references to `revokeSharesForItemsFn`, `revokeShares`, or `shares/revoke`.

---

### 3. Share Revocation Gap — CONFIRMED

- **In FUSE `spawn_bin_entry_publish()` (crates/fuse/src/metadata.rs:424):** Only publishes bin metadata to IPNS. Zero HTTP calls beyond IPFS/IPNS publish. **No authentication, no API calls, no share revocation.**
- **In SDK `addToBin()` (packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:483):** Calls `shareOps.revokeSharesForItems()` → `POST /shares/revoke-for-items` (packages/sdk/src/client.ts:226)
- **Result:** Files/folders deleted via desktop FUSE mount leave active `Share` + `ShareInvite` rows orphaned in the database. Sharees still have valid read access to deleted content (via IPFS CID pinned in their own vault or persisted elsewhere).

---

### 4. Hook Location & Fix Shape

**Where to add revocation (Rust side):**

Option A (Minimal): After `publish_bin_entry_on_delete()` in `handle_unlink`/`handle_rmdir`, spawn a separate HTTP call to `POST /shares/revoke-for-items` with the collected ipnsNames. Requires:
- Passing `ipnsNames` out of `publish_bin_entry_on_delete()` closure (currently discarded after bin entry is built)
- Rust HTTP client (already available: `cipherbox_api_client::*` used by `spawn_bin_entry_publish()`)
- User auth: `ApiClient` in `CipherBoxFS` already holds active auth context

Option B (Aligned with SDK): Make `spawn_bin_entry_publish()` accept a second closure `revokeSharesFn` (like SDK does), call it before bin publish, fail-closed if revoke fails. Requires refactoring the FUSE delete path to collect ipnsNames upfront (subtree walk for folders) and pass them through.

**Approx. size:** ~80-120 lines (Rust HTTP POST call + error handling + subtree walk for rmdir).

**Authentication:** Already available—`CipherBoxFS.api` is an authenticated `ApiClient` with user context.

---

### 5. Subtree Walk Capability

**For file deletes (`handle_unlink`):** Only file's own `fileMetaIpnsName` — trivial.

**For folder deletes (`handle_rmdir`):** Currently only deletes empty folders (POSIX requirement at line 237). To revoke nested shared content, would need:
- Recursive folder metadata walk (decrypt + read each child folder's metadata, same as SDK's `walkDeletedSubtree`)
- `folderKey` + `userPrivateKey` both available in `CipherBoxFS` scope
- Could reuse crypto functions from `cipherbox_core` / `cipherbox_crypto` (same as SDK uses)

**FUSE-specific constraint:** Single-threaded — the walk would need to be non-blocking (spawn background task like `spawn_bin_entry_publish` does) to avoid stalling the filesystem.

---

### Summary

**Desktop delete = hard orphan of shares.** The gap is **in the Rust FUSE handler**, not in a missing Tauri bridge. Share revocation must be added to `handle_unlink`/`handle_rmdir` (or the helper `publish_bin_entry_on_delete`) before the bin entry publish completes. The API infrastructure (`POST /shares/revoke-for-items`) and crypto keys exist; only the Rust-side call + subtree enumeration are missing.

## Desktop FUSE delete → share revocation: confirmed gap

**Desktop FUSE deletes bypass share revocation entirely.** The web/SDK fix in #563 lives only in `CipherBoxClient.addToBin`; desktop deletes go through a **parallel Rust-only path** that never touches it:

- `crates/fuse/src/write_ops/implementation/delete.rs:58` `handle_unlink` (file) / `:208` `handle_rmdir` (folder) → `publish_bin_entry_on_delete` → `spawn_bin_entry_publish` (`metadata.rs:424`).
- That path publishes a bin entry to IPNS but makes **zero API calls** — no auth, no `POST /shares/revoke-for-items`.
- **Result:** files/folders deleted from the desktop mount leave `Share` + `ShareInvite` rows active → sharees retain read access to deleted content. Same data-exposure bug #563 fixes for web, still open on desktop.

**Useful nuance:** the desktop fix is *simpler* than the SDK's — FUSE deletes bottom-up (`rmdir` requires empty, `delete.rs:237`), so each `unlink`/`rmdir` revokes exactly **one** node's `ipnsName`; no recursive `walkDeletedSubtree` needed. Auth (`CipherBoxFS.api`) and keys are already in scope. ~80-120 LOC Rust + tests.

  "content": "---\ncreated: 2026-06-26T00:00:00.000Z\ntitle: Desktop FUSE deletes bypass share revocation (and likely CID-capture)\narea: fuse\nseverity: high\nsource: Follow-up to PR #563 (web/SDK share-revocation-on-delete); user-flagged 2026-06-26 — desktop deletes leave shares active\nfiles:\n  - crates/fuse/src/write_ops/implementation/delete.rs\n  - crates/fuse/src/metadata.rs\n  - packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts\n  - packages/sdk/src/share/index.ts\n  - apps/api/src/shares/shares.controller.ts\n---\n\n## Problem\n\nPR #563 added fail-closed share revocation when an item is soft-deleted to the\nrecycle bin — but ONLY in the SDK/web path: `CipherBoxClient.addToBin`\n(`packages/sdk/src/client.ts`) injects `revokeSharesForItemsFn` into\n`binOps.addToBin` (`packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts`), which walks the deleted\nsubtree and calls `POST /shares/revoke-for-items` before the destructive folder\nmutation.\n\nDesktop (Tauri + FUSE) deletes go through a **parallel Rust-only path that never\ntouches that wiring**:\n\n- `crates/fuse/src/write_ops/implementation/delete.rs:58` `handle_unlink` (file)\n- `crates/fuse/src/write_ops/implementation/delete.rs:208` `handle_rmdir` (folder)\n- both call `publish_bin_entry_on_delete` → `spawn_bin_entry_publish`\n  (`crates/fuse/src/metadata.rs:424`)\n\nThat path publishes a `BinEntry` to the bin IPNS record but makes **zero API\ncalls beyond IPFS/IPNS** — no auth, no `POST /shares/revoke-for-items`. The FUSE\ncrate has no reference to `revokeSharesForItems` / `shares/revoke`.\n\n**Result:** any file/folder deleted from the desktop mount leaves its `Share` +\n`ShareInvite` rows active. Sharees retain valid read access to deleted content —\nthe exact data-exposure bug #563 closes for the web, still open on desktop.\n\n### Related sub-concern to verify (pin leak parity)\n\nThe #14 / #563 pin-leak fix (`unpinEntryCids`) only unpins CIDs that the\n`BinEntry` actually carries (`contentCid` / `versionCids` / `descendantCids`).\nConfirm whether the FUSE-built `BinEntry` in `spawn_bin_entry_publish` populates\nthose fields. If it does NOT, then content soft-deleted from desktop still leaks\npins on empty-bin/permanent-delete even after #563 — a second desktop parity gap\nto fix in the same pass.\n\n## Solution\n\nHook revocation into the Rust FUSE delete path, fail-closed, mirroring the SDK.\n\n1. **No subtree walk needed (simpler than SDK).** FUSE deletes bottom-up —\n   `rmdir` rejects non-empty dirs (`delete.rs:237`), so the OS unlinks each child\n   first. Each operation revokes exactly ONE node's `ipnsName`:\n   - `handle_unlink` → revoke the file's `fileMetaIpnsName`.\n   - `handle_rmdir` → revoke the (now-empty) folder's own `ipnsName`.\n2. **Infra already exists.** `CipherBoxFS.api` is an authenticated `ApiClient`\n   (already used by `spawn_bin_entry_publish`). Add a `POST /shares/revoke-for-items`\n   call with the node's `ipnsName`. `folderKey` + `userPrivateKey` are in\n   `CipherBoxFS` scope if any enumeration is needed.\n3. **Failure policy — design decision to lock.** The SDK aborts the delete if\n   revoke fails (it can, since it owns the publish). FUSE `unlink`/`rmdir` is a\n   filesystem op that is awkward to abort cleanly. Decide between: (a) block the\n   FUSE op until revoke succeeds (true fail-closed, but stalls the single-threaded\n   FUSE loop — must be careful), or (b) best-effort revoke with retries spawned\n   like `spawn_bin_entry_publish`, accepting a small window. Prefer fail-closed if\n   feasible without stalling; otherwise retried-best-effort with a logged alert.\n4. **Verify + fix CID capture** in the FUSE `BinEntry` (see sub-concern) so\n   empty-bin unpin works for desktop-deleted content too.\n5. **Test:** add a desktop E2E (or Rust integration assertion) that a shared file\n   deleted via the FUSE mount revokes its `Share` (and a folder rmdir revokes the\n   folder's own share). The desktop E2E is dispatch-gated — budget a CI round-trip.\n\nSize: ~80-120 LOC Rust + tests. Natural fit alongside the FUSE/desktop hardening\ncluster, or as a standalone `fix(fuse):` once #563 merges (its `/shares/revoke-for-items`\nendpoint is the dependency).\n"
}

+/**
+ * Extract an HTTP status code from an unknown caught error, if present.
+ *
+ * Handles both a flat `{ status }` shape and the axios `{ response: { status } }`
+ * shape used across the api-client.
+ *
+ * @param error - The caught error object
+ * @returns The numeric status code, or undefined if none can be determined
+ */
+export function getErrorStatus(error: unknown): number | undefined {
+  if (!error || typeof error !== 'object') return undefined;
+  const e = error as Record<string, unknown>;
+  if (typeof e.status === 'number') return e.status;
+  if (typeof e.response === 'object' && e.response !== null) {
+    const status = (e.response as Record<string, unknown>).status;
+    if (typeof status === 'number') return status;
+  }
+  return undefined;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Whether an error represents a deterministic client failure (4xx) that will
+ * never succeed on retry — e.g. a 400 validation rejection or a 401/403 auth
+ * failure. Transient errors (5xx, network errors with no status) remain retryable.
+ *
+ * @param error - The caught error object
+ * @returns true if the error is a non-retryable 4xx response
+ */
+export function isNonRetryableError(error: unknown): boolean {
+  const status = getErrorStatus(error);
+  return status !== undefined && status >= 400 && status < 500;
+}

The A1 chunking is **correct and fail-closed preserved**: `revokeSharesForItems` now slices into sequential ≤5000 batches via `revokeBatchWithRetry`, each batch must fully succeed before the next, and a final failure still throws → `addToBin` aborts the delete. The 4xx short-circuit (`isNonRetryableError`/`getErrorStatus` in `error.ts`) breaks the retry loop immediately on deterministic 4xx but still throws (just faster), keeping 5xx/network retryable — clean and consistent with the fail-closed contract. A partial-batch failure leaves "some shares revoked, item not deleted," which is the safe (recoverable) residual.

==================== 2026-06-23-fuse-resolve-sequence-legacy-parse-cas-base-zero.md ====================
---
created: 2026-06-23T23:40:00.000Z
title: FUSE non-strict resolve_sequence invents CAS base 0 on malformed legacy sequence
area: fuse
severity: low
resolves_phase: 60
source: PR #553 CodeRabbit Major (workflow-verified pre-existing) — 2026-06-23
files:
  - crates/fuse/src/publish.rs
---

## Problem

In `PublishCoordinator::resolve_sequence` (the non-strict path, `crates/fuse/src/publish.rs`
~114-124), the `VerifyError::Legacy` arm parses the carried `sequence_number` with
`.parse::<u64>().unwrap_or_else(|e| { warn; 0 })`, then `max(resolved, cached.unwrap_or(0))`.
On a parse failure with **no cached** sequence this returns `Ok(0)` — publishing from an invented
base — whereas the strict path (`resolve_sequence_strict`, ~182-184) returns `Err` on the same
parse failure. CodeRabbit flagged the strict-vs-non-strict asymmetry on PR #553.

## Why deferred (not fixed in Phase 59)

A parallel adversarial verifier confirmed (high confidence) this is **pre-existing**, not
introduced by Phase 59:

- `git show origin/main:crates/fuse/src/publish.rs` — the pre-phase non-strict Legacy arm already
  used the identical `parse().unwrap_or_else(0)` + `max(resolved, cached.unwrap_or(0))`. Phase 59
  only changed the **source** of the sequence string (carried `Legacy { sequence_number, .. }`
  instead of a second `resolve_ipns` call) to close a TOCTOU window (T-59-04); the 0-fallback
  semantics are byte-identical to `main`.
- Blast radius is low: `sequence_number` is the API's DB-stored numeric string (`verify.rs:71`), so
  a parse failure implies a corrupt/non-numeric DB value (practically never). Even then the publish
  carries `expected_sequence_number: Some("0")` and the server enforces CAS — a stale base returns
  `PublishResult::Conflict`, and the caller re-resolves + republishes with the correct base
  (`metadata.rs:140-161`). So base 0 cannot silently overwrite a newer record; it degrades to a
  benign conflict-retry.

Outside Phase 59's diff/scope → deferred rather than expanding scope.

## Solution (Phase 60)

Mirror the strict path's validation in `resolve_sequence`: on parse failure, return `Ok(cached)`
only when a cache entry exists, else `Err(...)` — do not invent base `0`.

```rust
let resolved = match sequence_number.parse::<u64>() {
    Ok(seq) => seq,
    Err(e) => {
        if let Some(cached) = self.get_cached(ipns_name) {
            log::warn!("Failed to parse carried IPNS sequence '{}' for {}, using cached seq {}: {}", sequence_number, ipns_name, cached, e);
            return Ok(cached);
        }
        return Err(format!("Invalid IPNS sequence '{}' for {} and no cached sequence: {}", sequence_number, ipns_name, e));
    }
};
```

No existing unit test exercises this parse-failure path, so the change is low-risk. Related:
`59-REVIEW.md`, PR #553 review thread on `publish.rs:120`.

==================== 2026-06-24-desktop-root-folder-publish-conflict-failfast.md ====================
---
created: 2026-06-24
title: Fail fast on root-folder publish conflict during desktop vault init
area: desktop
files:
  - apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/vault.rs
---

## Problem

In the desktop vault-init flow (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/vault.rs:182-187`), the root-folder publish `PublishResult::Conflict` arm only `log::warn!`s and falls through to `/vault/init` (step 3), whereas the analogous vault-key conflict arm (~line 139-142) returns `Err` and fails fast. The asymmetry means an unexpected conflict on the first root-folder publish (sequence 1) is silently swallowed and initialization continues on inconsistent state.

Surfaced by CodeRabbit during the Phase 60 ship review (finding F10). Verified real but **pre-existing** (not introduced by Phase 60 — Phase 60 only changed the embedded sequence 0→1 here), so classified out-of-scope for the strict-cutover phase.

## Solution

Mirror the vault-key conflict path: in the root-folder publish `PublishResult::Conflict { .. }` arm, `return Err("Vault initialization aborted due to existing root folder IPNS record")` (or equivalent) so init fails fast instead of proceeding to `/vault/init`.

==================== 2026-06-24-fuse-metadata-unpin-orphaned-cid-on-verify-fail.md ====================
---
created: 2026-06-24
title: Unpin the orphaned uploaded CID when verified merge fails closed
area: fuse
files:
  - crates/fuse/src/metadata.rs
---

## Problem

In `spawn_metadata_publish` (`crates/fuse/src/metadata.rs`), the new metadata blob (`new_cid`) is uploaded and server-pinned (~line 245) before the verified-resolve/merge step. Every normal exit of the Conflict arm unpins `new_cid` (Success ~line 391, persistent-Conflict ~line 403), but the `VerifyError::Invalid` fail-closed branch (~line 327-330) returns early **without** unpinning, leaving an orphaned pinned blob on every retry of a verification failure.

Surfaced by CodeRabbit during the Phase 60 ship review (finding F11). Verified real but classified out-of-scope (it is a storage-cleanup leak, not a verification-correctness gap — the fail-closed behavior itself is correct) and not low-risk (touches the delicate merge flow).

## Solution

In the `VerifyError::Invalid` arm of the verified merge, call `cipherbox_api_client::ipfs::unpin_content(&api, &new_cid)` (best-effort, same as the other exits) before returning the error, so a failed IPNS verify does not strand the pre-uploaded blob.
```

==================== 2026-06-18-gsd-phase-complete-regresses-state-final-phase.md ====================
---
created: 2026-06-18
title: gsd-tools `phase complete` regresses STATE.md body on a milestone's final phase
area: tooling
files:
  - .claude/gsd-core/bin/lib/state.cjs
  - .planning/STATE.md
---

## Problem

Running `gsd-tools phase complete <N>` on the LAST phase of a milestone updates
the frontmatter correctly (`status: Milestone complete`, `completed_phases`,
`percent`) but silently corrupts two `## Current Position` body lines and the
velocity headline.

Observed 2026-06-18 on PR #512 (commit `21cfd78dc`):

- `Plan: 5 of 5 — COMPLETE` was rewritten to `Plan: Not started`.
- The phase line lost its `— COMPLETE` marker (`Phase: 49 (...) — COMPLETE`
  became bare `Phase: 49`).
- `- Total plans completed: 182 (72 M1 + 83 M2 + 6 M3)` was bumped to `199` —
  a value matching neither its own breakdown (`72 + 83 + 6 = 161`) nor the real
  audited count (`151`).

CodeRabbit flagged both the `Not started` inconsistency and the `199` mismatch;
both were artifacts of this regression, fixed by hand in `a3986cc9c` (velocity →
audited `151`) and `a7e8bd80e` (Current Position restored).

## Root cause

In `.claude/gsd-core/bin/lib/state.cjs`, the `## Current Position` sync
(`updateCurrentPositionFields`) and the velocity-total writer only run as a
side-effect of `begin-phase` / `advance-plan` on an ACTIVE phase. There is no
milestone-complete path that resets the body to a terminal state, so completing
the final phase leaves these lines stale or regressed. `query validate.health`
reports `healthy` and does not catch it (existing-STATE content drift is
non-repairable by design).

## Solution

TBD. Options to evaluate:

- Teach `phase complete` (when it is the milestone's last phase) to write a
  terminal Current Position (`Phase: N (...) — COMPLETE`, `Plan: M of M —
  COMPLETE`) and recompute the velocity total from the current milestone's
  `*-SUMMARY.md` count, instead of the cumulative `begin-phase` increment.
- Add a `validate.health` check that compares the velocity "Total plans
  completed" headline against the disk audit (`*-PLAN.md` / `*-SUMMARY.md` per
  milestone phase) and flags drift.
- At minimum, document that the STATE.md body is not authoritative after a
  milestone completes — the frontmatter `progress` block is.

## Notes

- Authoritative count is the frontmatter `total_plans`/`completed_plans` plus a
  disk audit; for v1.1 all four sources agreed at `151` (34 phases, every PLAN
  has a SUMMARY).

---

## Summary

The Phase 53 Cargo.lock release-sync step (`release-please.yml`, `cargo-lock-sync`)
loops over each released first-party crate and runs
`cargo update -p <pkg> --precise <ver>`. This is deliberate (D-05: first-party
only, no transitive re-resolution) and works because each crate's checked-out
`Cargo.toml` already declares the bumped version, so `--precise` is effectively a
no-op match that just refreshes the lock's `[[package]]` line.

## Consideration (deferred — design change, not a bug)

If a crate's `Cargo.toml` version and the release-please output `<ver>` ever
disagree (e.g. a partial/timing-skewed release), `cargo update --precise <ver>`
errors out and fails the release job. A single `cargo update --workspace` (or
`cargo generate-lockfile`) would re-sync all workspace members directly from their
manifests in one shot, and the existing `git diff --exit-code Cargo.lock` guard
would still validate the result.

## Why deferred

Switching to `--workspace` changes the documented design intent (it re-resolves
the whole tree rather than touching only released first-party crates). That is a
behavioral change to release automation, not a safe in-place simplification — it
should be evaluated against a real release-please cycle, not slipped into a ship
pass. Captured for a future release-automation hardening pass. The current
per-crate approach passes all Phase 53 gates and is correct for the current
manifest/Cargo.toml state.

## Source

Raised during Phase 53 ship-phase simplify review (CodeRabbit/simplify pass).

  - .github/workflows/ci.yml

## Summary

`desktop-staging-release.yml` installs the FUSE-T pkg-config file via
`sudo ln -sf "$FUSE_T_PC" /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig/fuse.pc` (a symlink), whereas
the macOS Cargo job in `ci.yml` uses `sudo cp "$FUSE_T_PC" .../fuse.pc` and then
rewrites `Version:` in place (to `2.9.9`). The staging workflow's symlink path
skips that version rewrite and the existence check ci.yml guards with.

## Why deferred (NOT a Phase 53 change)

This is PRE-EXISTING — Phase 53 only SHA-pinned `uses:` refs and added
`permissions:` blocks in `desktop-staging-release.yml`; it did not touch the
`ln -sf` / `fuse.pc` install line. Out of scope for the release-supply-chain
phase (this is desktop FUSE build-env, not supply-chain hardening). Raised by
greptile (P2) on PR #531; capturing for a future desktop-CI consistency pass.

## Fix direction (future)

Align the staging workflow with ci.yml: `cp` the pc file + rewrite `Version:` +
add the existence guard, so the two macOS FUSE build paths are identical and a
version-string mismatch can't fail the Cargo build only on staging.

## Source

greptile review thread on PR #531 (path desktop-staging-release.yml:29).

==================== 2026-06-20-tsconfig-scripts-hardcoded-types-node-version.md ====================
---
created: 2026-06-20
title: Remove hardcoded @types/node version from tsconfig.scripts.json typeRoots
area: test-infra
phase: 55-or-later
files:
  - tsconfig.scripts.json
---

## Problem

`tsconfig.scripts.json` (added in Phase 54 plan 01) pins a version-specific `typeRoots` entry:

```json
"typeRoots": [
  "./node_modules/@types",
  "./node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@22.19.7/node_modules/@types"
]
```

The `@types+node@22.19.7` path will break the `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json --noEmit` step (wired into root `pnpm typecheck`) when `@types/node` is bumped.

## Why it was deferred (not fixed inline during Phase 54 ship)

The obvious fixes do NOT work in this pnpm layout (empirically tested):

- Removing `typeRoots` entirely → `error TS2688: Cannot find type definition file for 'node'` (pnpm does not hoist `@types/node` to root `node_modules/@types/`; there is no `node_modules/@types/node`).
- Glob `./node_modules/.pnpm/@types+node@*/node_modules/@types` → same TS2688 (TypeScript does not expand `*` in `typeRoots`).

There are 4 `@types/node` versions in the store (`12.20.55`, `20.19.37`, `22.7.5`, `22.19.7`); the config must point at a concrete one. The pin matches the lockfile-resolved version, so it is correct today, just fragile on upgrade.

## Solution

Robust fix is a small dependency change (out of Phase 54's low-risk scope): declare `@types/node` as a direct root devDependency so pnpm hoists `node_modules/@types/node`, then the standard `./node_modules/@types` entry resolves it with no version pin and the `.pnpm` line can be dropped. Validate the existing 4 versions don't conflict, then run `pnpm typecheck`. Alternatively, add a CI check that fails if the pinned version drifts from the lockfile.
```

Read all four. Here's where I land:

## #7 (Cargo.lock release sync) — what it is, and my take: **leave it deferred**

In plain terms: the Rust crates live in a Cargo workspace, and `Cargo.lock` pins exact versions. When release-please bumps a crate's version in its `Cargo.toml`, the lockfile must be re-synced or CI's "lock in sync" check fails. The current release workflow does this **surgically** — loops over each released first-party crate and runs `cargo update -p <crate> --precise <ver>`, deliberately *not* re-resolving third-party/transitive deps (a conscious supply-chain decision: only touch our own crates).

The todo's concern is a theoretical edge: if a crate's `Cargo.toml` version and release-please's computed version ever disagree (a partial/timing-skewed release), `--precise` errors and fails the job. The proposed alternative — `cargo update --workspace` — re-syncs everything in one shot but **re-resolves the whole dependency tree**, which is exactly what the current design avoids.

**My recommendation: don't implement it.** It's not a bug — the current approach is correct and passes all release gates. The "fix" trades a practically-never edge case for a real downside (whole-tree re-resolution / supply-chain surface), and it's a release-automation behavior change that should only be validated against a *real* release cycle, never slipped into a batch. Good instinct to question it — revisit only if an actual release fails on that skew.

## #5 (gsd-tools STATE.md regression) — I'm holding this one too

It's the odd one out: its solution is explicitly **TBD** (three competing options), and the real fix would patch `.claude/gsd-core/bin/lib/state.cjs` — which is **vendored** third-party `@opengsd/gsd-core` code that gets overwritten on the next tool update. So a local patch is fragile, and the alternatives (a health-check vs just documenting that the STATE.md body isn't authoritative post-milestone) are a design call, not a mechanical fix. **Not a clean autonomous-batch item** — it needs a decision from you first. I left it out.

  "content": "---\ncreated: 2026-06-26T00:00:00.000Z\ntitle: Revoke shares on rename/replace-over-existing-destination (web + desktop)\narea: fuse\nseverity: high\nsource: PR #568 adversarial review (revocation-completeness lens) — 2026-06-26\nfiles:\n  - crates/fuse/src/write_ops/implementation/rename.rs\n  - crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/write_ops.rs\n  - packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts\n  - packages/sdk/src/client.ts\n  - apps/api/src/shares/shares.controller.ts\n---\n\n## Problem\n\nPRs #563 (web/SDK) and #568 (desktop FUSE) added fail-closed share revocation on\n**delete** — but only on the delete-to-bin path. When a file/folder is **renamed\nor moved OVER an existing destination** (replace/overwrite), the destination node\nis destroyed WITHOUT revoking its shares. This is the same data-exposure class as\nthe delete bug those PRs closed: the destination's `Share` / `ShareInvite` rows\nstay active against content that has been replaced (and, on the unix file branch,\nits CID is even unpinned), so sharees retain read access to vanished content.\n\nConfirmed by the #568 completeness review as **pre-existing on every surface**:\n\n- **Unix FUSE:** `crates/fuse/src/write_ops/implementation/rename.rs` (~163-186) —\n  the File branch destroys the dest node and even spawns `unpin_content` on the\n  dest CID, with no share revocation.\n- **Windows FUSE:** `crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/write_ops.rs` (~1097-1124) —\n  same replace-over-dest path, no revocation.\n- **Web / SDK:** the #563 revocation (`revokeSharesForItemsFn`) is wired ONLY into\n  `addToBin` (`packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:483`, `client.ts:221`), NOT into any\n  overwrite/replace/move path.\n\nSo there is NO web-vs-desktop parity regression — it's an equal gap on both, and\n#568 correctly scoped rename out (delete-only).\n\n## Solution\n\nWhen a rename/move overwrites an existing destination, revoke the **destination\nnode's** shares before/as the destination is destroyed, mirroring the delete-path\nfail-closed contract (`POST /shares/revoke-for-items`, revoke-before-destructive-\nmutation, abort on failure where the call site allows it):\n\n1. **Web/SDK:** wire revocation into the replace/overwrite path (whatever the SDK\n   uses when a move/upload clobbers an existing destination), reusing the existing\n   `revokeSharesForItems` helper + chunking + 4xx short-circuit.\n2. **Unix FUSE** (`rename.rs`): revoke the dest node's `ipnsName`\n   (`file_meta_ipns_name` for a file dest) before destroying it; reuse\n   `metadata::revoke_shares_blocking` (added in #568). ## #568 — reviews resolved ✓
**CodeRabbit was rate-limited (0 findings); Greptile raised 2 P2s, both handled:**

- **Finding 2 — `handle_unlink` double inode lookup** → **fixed**: collapsed into a single `match` carrying out both the revoke name and bin data (mirrors `handle_rmdir`), dead `EISDIR`/`ENOENT` arms removed. Behavior-preserving; tests pass.
- **Finding 1 — Windows premature revocation on a *cancelled* delete** → **documented as a deliberate trade-off** (Greptile's own fallback ask was "document it"). Worth you knowing the semantics: on Windows, `set_delete` is the *only* callback that can reject a delete (fail-closed); `handle_cleanup` can't. So revoking in `set_delete` means a `set_delete(true)`→cancel sequence **over-revokes** shares for an item that ends up *not* deleted. That's the **safe direction** — "shares revoked but item remains" is recoverable (re-share), whereas the alternative (revoke in cleanup) would be best-effort and risk the actual data-exposure. Accepted + documented; the green Windows gate is authoritative.

Commit `a493ef660` (signed), cargo green locally (24 api-client + 104 fuse tests), **0 unresolved threads**.
